title: Dividing a Whole Number by a Unit Fraction
short: 4 ÷ 1/2 asks how many halves fit in 4.
trouble: Children believe division always makes a number smaller, so they answer 4 ÷ 1/2 = 2.

blocks.html: You have shared a unit fraction among people. Now turn it around: how many pieces of size $\frac{1}{2}$ fit in 4 wholes? That is $4 \div \frac{1}{2}$.
$n \div \frac{1}{b} = n \times b$. Each whole holds $b$ pieces of size $\frac{1}{b}$, so $n$ wholes hold $n \times b$ of them. $4 \div \frac{1}{2} = 8$.

Division can ask “how many groups of this size fit?”: $12 \div 3$ asks how many 3s fit in 12. In the same way, $4 \div \frac{1}{2}$ asks how many halves fit in 4. There are 2 halves in each whole, so there are 8 in 4. Check: $8 \times \frac{1}{2} = 4$.

blocks.name: numberline
blocks.cap: Jumps of $\frac{1}{2}$ from 0 to 4: eight jumps, so $4 \div \frac{1}{2} = 8$.

blocks.title: Servings
blocks.q: How many $\frac{1}{3}$-cup servings are in 5 cups of rice?

blocks.html: Believing division always makes a number smaller, so $4 \div \frac{1}{2} = 2$. That answer is $4 \div 2$, splitting 4 into 2 groups. Dividing by a number less than 1 asks how many small pieces fit, and the answer is bigger. Check: $2 \times \frac{1}{2} = 1$, not 4.
